title: Design and Modular Verification of Distributed Transactions in MongoDB
formal_method: TLA+; TLC explicit-state model checking; model-based test generation
main_contribution: modular formal specification of MongoDB distributed transactions and storage-interface conformance testing
method: TLA+ model checking plus TLC-generated storage test cases executed against WiredTiger
main_result: verified isolation properties on bounded models and checked storage-interface implementation behavior
main_limitation: small finite models; published model-based testing does not exercise concurrently executing clients
gap_vs_dtl_lab: No Alloy or scientific mutant catalogue; implementation check is model-generated storage testing rather than valid/negative trace conformance; no independent reproduction comparable to Phase 8E
notes: Closest domain comparator identified so far.

title: Validating Traces of Distributed Programs Against TLA+ Specifications
authors: Horatiu Cirstea; Markus A. Kuppe; Benjamin Loillier; Stephan Merz
main_contribution: general framework for validating partial implementation traces against high-level TLA+ specifications
method: Java instrumentation plus trace specification and constrained TLC model checking
main_result: detected discrepancies across multiple distributed-system case studies
main_limitation: incomplete traces trade lower instrumentation for larger search and can be accepted incorrectly if too little information is logged
gap_vs_dtl_lab: General trace-validation method, not a cross-shard study; no Alloy, mutant layer, frozen multiseed valid/negative campaign, or independent artifact reproduction
notes: DLT-Lab must not claim Java-to-TLA+ trace validation as method novelty.

title: TraceLinking Implementations with Their Verified Designs
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages OOPSLA2
main_contribution: automated trace linking between PGo-generated implementations and verified designs
method: compiler-supported instrumentation; generated TLA+ trace interpretation; one-path, all-paths and sidestep validation
main_result: found nine previously undetected bugs across three distributed systems
main_limitation: automation depends on PGo/MPCal assumptions; one raftkvs all-paths validation exceeded 12 hours
gap_vs_dtl_lab: Not cross-shard; no Alloy or mutation-based property layer; implementation is compiler-generated from the formal source whereas DTL-Lab validates an independently implemented Java protocol
notes: Antithesis reproduced part of the experiments; independent reproduction has partial scope.

title: Towards Strengthening Formal Specifications with Mutation Model Checking
authors: Maxime Cordy; Sami Lazreg; Axel Legay; Pierre Yves Schobbens
main_contribution: mutation model checking to assess and strengthen formal specifications
method: syntactic Promela mutation plus SPIN checks and mutation-score analysis
main_result: existing specifications killed about 60 percent and 40 percent of generated mutants in two case studies
main_limitation: preliminary five-page NIER; proposed strengthening framework not yet fully operational
gap_vs_dtl_lab: Not blockchain; no TLA+ or Alloy experiments; broad syntactic mutants rather than a small protocol-targeted scientific mutant catalogue
notes: DLT-Lab applies mutation-based validation but does not synthesize stronger properties.

title: Technical Report: Exploring Automatic Model-Checking of the Ethereum specification
authors: Igor Konnov; Jure Kukovec; Thomas Pani; Roberto Saltini; Thanh Hai Tran
main_contribution: multi-formalism automated model checking and abstraction study for Ethereum 3SF AccountableSafety
method: manual translation from executable Python spec; TLA+ abstractions; Apalache, CVC5 and Alloy experiments
main_result: bounded AccountableSafety verification for small instances; deliberate bugs yield counterexamples; larger configurations exhibit severe cost and timeouts
main_limitation: technical report; bounded small instances; runtime variance and very long timeouts; no implementation trace conformance
gap_vs_dtl_lab: Not cross-shard transactions; no runtime implementation-model conformance or independent reproduction comparable to Phase 8E; however it already combines TLA+, Alloy, deliberate defects and verification-cost experiments
notes: Critical comparator that narrows DTL-Lab integration novelty.

title: Smart Casual Verification of the Confidential Consortium Framework
authors: Heidi Howard; Markus A. Kuppe; Edward Ashton; Amaury Chamayou; Natacha Crooks
system_domain: production distributed consensus and client consistency
formal_method: TLA+; TLC model checking; simulation; trace validation
main_contribution: smart casual verification tying TLA+ specifications to a production C++ implementation and CI
method: model checking, simulation, automated testing and implementation trace validation
main_result: found six subtle safety and liveness bugs before production and integrated validation into CI
main_limitation: substantial initial trace-validation engineering effort; not a cross-shard transaction study
gap_vs_dtl_lab: No Alloy or mutation-based property layer and no independent reproduction comparable to Phase 8E; much stronger continuous production integration
notes: Critical comparator for TLA+ plus implementation trace validation plus CI.

title: Protocol Conformance with Choreographic PlusCal
authors: Darius Foo; Andreea Costea; Wei-Ngan Chin
formal_method: Choreographic PlusCal; TLA+; TLC; generated monitors
main_contribution: choreographic protocol specification and compilation of TLA+ models into conformance monitors
method: project choreography to PlusCal/TLA+ and execute generated Go monitors on observed implementation behavior
main_result: demonstrated low monitoring overhead on a 2PC implementation and etcd
main_limitation: monitoring is sound but incomplete and depends on executed assertions and faithful instrumentation
gap_vs_dtl_lab: Not blockchain cross-shard; no Alloy, mutation layer, controlled valid/negative multiseed trace corpus or independent reproduction
notes: Direct methodological comparator for 2PC implementation conformance.

title: Verifying Zookeeper based on Model-Based runtime Trace-Checking using TLA+
authors: Zhi Niu; Luming Dong; Yong Zhu; Li Chen
main_contribution: runtime trace checking of ZooKeeper against a TLA+ model
method: full text not recovered during G4; no detailed method claims retained
main_result: not used for substantive comparison because full text was unavailable
main_limitation: primary full text unavailable during screening
notes: Metadata verified; retain for snowballing only.

title: Model Checking Guided Testing for Distributed Systems
authors: Dong Wang; Wensheng Dou; Yu Gao; Chenao Wu; Jun Wei; Tao Huang
formal_method: TLA+; model checking guided systematic testing
main_contribution: use verified TLA+ state spaces to systematically test distributed-system implementations
method: generate tests from verified abstract states, force Java executions and compare runtime states with formal states
main_result: found three previously unknown implementation bugs, four known bugs and two specification bugs
main_limitation: manual modelling and mapping effort; coverage depends on abstraction and mapped actions
gap_vs_dtl_lab: Not cross-shard blockchain; no Alloy or mutation property validation; stronger state-space-driven implementation testing but no independent reproduction badge
notes: EuroSys artifact has Artifacts Available badge but not Results Reproduced.

title: Model Checking Guided Incremental Testing for Distributed Systems
authors: Yu Gao; Dong Wang; Wensheng Dou; Wenhan Feng; Yu Liang; Yuan Feng; Jun Wei
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering ISSTA 2025
formal_method: TLA+; model checking guided incremental testing
method: identify affected formal state space and generate implementation tests focused on changed states and transitions
main_result: 74.83 percent average test-case reduction and 22.54 to 99.99 percent testing-time reduction across 12 change scenarios
main_limitation: cannot automatically detect some changes outside mapped actions or concurrency changes; potentially high state-graph cost
gap_vs_dtl_lab: Methodological evolution of Mocket, not a cross-shard validation study and no Alloy, mutation-property layer or independent reproduction
notes: Useful as recent state of the art for implementation-model testing efficiency.

title: Using Lightweight Formal Methods to Validate a Key-Value Storage Node in Amazon S3
authors: James Bornholt; Rajeev Joshi; Vytautas Astrauskas; Brendan Cully; Bernhard Kragl; Seth Markle; Kyle Sauri; Drew Schleit; Grant Slatton; Serdar Tasiran; Jacob Van Geffen; Andrew Warfield
formal_method: executable Rust reference models; property-based testing; failure injection; stateless model checking
main_contribution: pragmatic multi-technique validation workflow around executable reference models for a production storage system
method: decompose correctness properties and apply property-based testing, failure injection and stateless model checking against reference models
main_result: prevented 16 issues from reaching production and enabled maintenance by non-formal-methods engineers
main_limitation: lightweight testing and model checking remain incomplete; selected properties and reference models do not cover all system behavior
gap_vs_dtl_lab: Not blockchain cross-shard; no TLA+ or Alloy study, no mutation property validation, no trace-conformance experiment or independent reproduction
notes: Strong comparator against any broad claim that multi-technique implementation validation is novel.

title: Chainspace: A Sharded Smart Contracts Platform
authors: Mustafa Al-Bassam; Alberto Sonnino; Shehar Bano; Dave Hrycyszyn; George Danezis
formal_method: theorem-based S-BAC consistency and validity arguments
main_contribution: S-BAC distributed atomic commit protocol for sharded smart contracts
method: BFT shard coordination, correctness theorems, Java/BFT-SMaRt prototype and performance evaluation
main_result: atomic cross-shard transaction processing with measured scalability and throughput
main_limitation: prototype and bounded deployment evaluation; evidence differs from executable model checking and implementation-model conformance
gap_vs_dtl_lab: No TLA+, Alloy, mutation-property validation, trace conformance, verification-cost study or independent reproduction comparable to DTL-Lab
notes: Seminal domain comparator; theorem-based correctness must not be described as no verification.

title: OmniLedger: A Secure, Scale-Out, Decentralized Ledger via Sharding
authors: Eleftherios Kokoris-Kogias; Philipp Jovanovic; Linus Gasser; Nicolas Gailly; Ewa Syta; Bryan Ford
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
formal_method: informal security argument for Atomix; protocol analysis
main_contribution: Atomix client-driven atomic cross-shard transaction protocol within OmniLedger
method: lock/unlock proofs across input and output shards, Go prototype, DeterLab performance evaluation
main_result: secure scale-out sharding architecture with atomic cross-shard transaction handling and measured performance
main_limitation: Atomix security is argued informally and liveness can depend on another entity completing the protocol after client failure
gap_vs_dtl_lab: No TLA+, Alloy, mutation layer, implementation-model trace conformance, verification-cost characterization or independent reproduction
notes: Seminal Atomix comparator; performance metrics are not verification-cost metrics.

title: Prophet: Conflict-Free Sharding Blockchain via Byzantine-Tolerant Deterministic Ordering
authors: Zicong Hong; Song Guo; Enyuan Zhou; Jianting Zhang; Wuhui Chen; Jinwen Liang; Jie Zhang; Albert Y. Zomaya
formal_method: analytical proofs of deterministic ordering and serializability
main_contribution: Byzantine-tolerant deterministic ordering to reduce cross-shard conflicts and aborts
method: ordering architecture, correctness proofs, Geth-based Go prototype and distributed performance experiments
main_result: reported up to 3.11x throughput and nearly eliminated aborts in the evaluated workload
main_limitation: focuses on protocol execution efficiency rather than a multi-layer formal validation workflow
gap_vs_dtl_lab: No TLA+, Alloy, mutation-property validation, trace conformance, verification-cost characterization or verified independent reproduction
notes: Protocol-performance comparator; artifact availability remained unclear.

title: Cross shard leader accountability protocol based on two phase atomic commit
authors: Zhiqiang Du; Wendong Zhang; Liangxin Liu; et al.
formal_method: analytical consistency and liveness theorems; time and communication complexity analysis
main_contribution: leader-accountability protocol layered on two-phase atomic commit
method: protocol theorems, complexity analysis, Go simulation and Alibaba Cloud experiments
main_result: reports lower communication latency while preserving stated consistency and liveness properties
main_limitation: single-protocol simulation rather than a full sharded blockchain and a synchronous network assumption
gap_vs_dtl_lab: No TLA+, Alloy, model checking, mutation-property validation, implementation-model trace conformance or independent reproduction
notes: Public code is explicitly linked by the paper.

title: Presto: Optimizing Cross-Shard Transactions in Sharded Blockchain Architecture
authors: Qiuyu Ding; Rongkai Zhang; Shenglin Yin; Pengze Li; Shengjie Guan; Zhen Xiao; Jieyi Long
formal_method: unclear; full text not recovered during G5
main_contribution: optimistic pre-execution and pending-tree techniques for cross-shard transaction latency
method: abstract reports optimistic pre-execution, pending tree, erasure-coded predistribution and cloud prototype evaluation
main_result: abstract reports improvements in throughput, confirmation latency and mempool queue size
main_limitation: primary full text unavailable during G5, preventing strong methodological comparison
gap_vs_dtl_lab: Not assessed beyond verified metadata and abstract
notes: Do not infer absence of formal techniques from the abstract.

title: LightCross: Sharding with Lightweight Cross-Shard Execution for Smart Contracts
formal_method: theorem-based atomicity, serializability and liveness proofs
main_contribution: TEE-assisted lightweight cross-shard execution and commit protocol
method: correctness theorems, FISCO-BCOS prototype, Ethereum-derived workloads and scalability experiments
main_result: reports up to 2.6x throughput with atomicity, serializability and liveness arguments
main_limitation: focuses on protocol correctness and runtime performance rather than executable formal-model validation
gap_vs_dtl_lab: No TLA+, Alloy, mutation-property validation, implementation-model trace conformance, verification-cost characterization or independent reproduction
notes: Theorem-based correctness is explicit and must be represented accurately.
